items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: I work with majority of them... Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon. My last recording on the deck. Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon.

ctx.x: Hold on, I don't hurt, the storm won't hurt that I don't think. Well, that kind of... Instead of picking up all the rain, you hear the rain on here and the, uh, thunder. I guess that won't be the tornado they predicted maybe anyway, we hope not.

So, them kind of fellas, I can tell you a lot about them, because I know them, I work with majority of them. Now we couldn't come to Jimmy Noon. I work with Jimmy Noon. My last recording on the deck was, you remember, with Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon and everybody. Johnny Dotson. My last recording on the deck. Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon's a good musician. Read clarinet parts like nobody's business. I mean clarinet parts. And Johnny Dots could read clarinet parts. Very few clarinet parts you can find read…
Barney is your cousin. My cousin.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: Johnny Dots, David Dots and myself. Didn't you read Johnny? Each one had a rubber cloth that thick. And we had arrangements to it.

ctx.x: New Orleans? Born and raised in New Orleans. What town? I was born on Lakewood Street, 1719 Lakewood Street. That's the 7th Ward. In the year of 1894. August the 2nd. What musicians did you play with when you were? In New Orleans? I played with my teacher's band. Orchestra, I mean. Man Perez, he died in the mandolin toilet. And I played with different artists with Robichardt. Different artists. Were they strictly reading bands? Oh yeah. The band, the little accommodation that we had. Johnny Dots, David Dots and…

He didn't care about nobody. George Wettling. George Wettling tried to play like me. Dave Teuf tried to play like me. But there's only one drummer I let come on the bandstand to play. That was Downward.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: Baby daughter, Johnny daughter, I mean. ... Man, they know all over the world. They know what kind of drummer he is, what kind of musician he is.

ctx.x: He said, you got a record of the top of my heart. I was supposed to. I know, he's nearly as tall as I am. He said, all the men have music. Sonny Gray was there.

So, I said, Ben, what do you want to play? I said, Duke, what are you going to play? I can't play no numbers. He said, just play in the numbers. He said, I'll play some. He picked up a number. So, I told Dave, I said, oh, Dave, you don't want no music to hear? He said, no. He said, no. And here's Dave, that's here. I always put him on there. Here's Sonny Gray on. Here's this side. Look at that. Look at that. That's that drummer that the government. So, man, we struck up. I made a double-fought introduction. Loud.…
I thought he played that Spanish number. Duke. I was standing right alongside Baby Dots, looking at that music. He said, now, if I could get that man, I'd be on top of the world.
